title: catalog-quickstart-skeletal-wires-and-copy-heuristics
summary: Working sketch for a condensed catalog quickstart flow: single-page endpoint creation + optional version pinning microflow. Purpose is to reduce cognitive load for first-time users and provide inline microcopy that explains the tradeoffs of pinning vs. floating routes.
goals: Make "create endpoint" path approachable for engineers who just want a quick test endpoint
Surface default safety and cost tradeoffs in small chunks rather than a full config page
Give a short, reversible path to pin a model version with clear guidance and fallback behaviour
Keep default latency/cost defaults conservative but show advanced toggles for power users
personas: Product engineer: wants a working endpoint in <10 minutes to demo a prototype
Platform engineer: cares about predictable behaviour and wants explicit pinning for reproducibility
Data scientist: will iterate on model versions and wants easy compare + rollback
wireframe_descriptions: Top strip: project selector + lightweight breadcrumb (Project > Models > Quickstart). Small help icon opens inline tips rather than a full modal.
Main left column: Catalog quick search (algolia-like), suggested models list (curated for onboarding), each card shows latency/cost estimate and a small "pin" toggle with tooltip.

Main right column: Live endpoint preview panel. Shows endpoint name, selected model, example prompt input, 'Run' button and real-time token cost estimate. Below: quick logs (last 5 runs) and simple latency histogram.

Inline pin microflow: When user flips pin toggle, we show a single-line confirmation strip: 'Pinning locks to model X @ v2.0 — updates won't change this endpoint. You can unpin later from the endpoint settings.' Primary action 'Confirm pin' secondary 'Cancel'. No full page required.

Advanced toggle (collapsed by default): reveals tuning options: concurrency target, max tokens default, batch window ms, quantization options (recommended/experimental). Each item has an inline 'why this matters' microcopy.
Error/empty states: If no models match search, show 'Try our curated sample models' with one-click 'Use sample' that auto-selects a recommended tiny model and pre-fills a safe example prompt.

Footer: small checklist with three items before 'Create endpoint': 1) Name chosen, 2) Model selected, 3) Billing plan compatible. If any missing, create button disabled with tooltip explaining which item is incomplete.
copy_snippets: Endpoint name placeholder: 'give this endpoint a descriptive name — e.g., 'chat-assistant-staging''
Model card microcopy: 'Estimated latency: 60–120ms · Cost per 1k tokens: $0.004 (varies by prompt)'
Pin toggle tooltip: 'Lock this endpoint to a specific model version so responses stay stable across updates. Useful for reproducible behavior and audits.'
Pin confirmation strip: 'Pin to v2.0 — This endpoint will always use v2.0 unless you unpin. Pins are reversible but require a deploy.'
Run button microcopy (rate limited): 'Rate limit hit — try again in 12s or increase reserved capacity'
Advanced toggle label: 'More controls (for power users)'
Empty search hint: 'No matches — try broadening the model family or use a curated sample.'
Create CTA when ready: 'Create endpoint — Start testing'
grooming_notes: Sprint grooming 2024-11-07: agree to land skeleton quickstart as MLP (minimum lovable product) — exclude RBAC and enterprise-only KMS fields for initial drop. Scope: UI + client-side validations + a1 telemetry events. Next steps: prototype in Figma, hand off to FE for HTML wireframe, add acceptance tests in Cypress.
backlog_items: UX-001: Implement single-page quickstart layout (search + preview)
UX-002: Add pin toggle with confirmation strip and basic audit event
ENG-014: Surface model latency/cost estimates from catalog API
ENG-018: Implement client-side validation for billing compatibility checks
SRE-006: Ensure preview runs are routed to sandbox capacity and not counted against production quotas
acceptance_criteria: Create CTA enabled only when name + model selected + billing compatible
Pin action emits analytics event 'endpoint.pin.confirm' and stores pin in endpoint metadata
Preview run uses sandbox routing and returns within expected SLO (<500ms P95) for tiny models
Advanced controls are hidden by default and expand/collapse state persists per user
open_questions: Should pin confirmation require an extra typed confirmation for enterprise customers? (security/legal ask)
Do we expose the exact model digest/hash in the UI or keep it behind 'version label' for simplicity?
What is the default behavior when a pinned model is deprecated — auto-fallback to family or blocked?
Telemetry: what minimum data do we record to link a regression alert to a specific pinned endpoint?
